traitReasons.pavedEfficiency: Road R1's narrow tires, rigid chassis and road-focused cockpit prioritize efficient paved riding.
traitReasons.mixedSurface: Road R1 can tolerate limited rough surfaces, but that is not its primary design target.
traitReasons.technicalTerrain: Road R1 lacks the tire volume, geometry and suspension intended for technical trail riding.
traitReasons.distanceEfficiency: Its riding position and road-oriented rolling setup are built around sustained distance efficiency.
traitReasons.climbingCapability: Low rolling losses and an efficient road drivetrain suit sustained paved climbing.
traitReasons.comfortControl: Road R1 favors efficiency and direct response over rough-terrain control and impact isolation.
traitReasons.cargoUtility: The current Road R1 reference has no dedicated cargo or utility architecture.
traitReasons.allWeather: Disc brakes help, but the reference bike is not a dedicated all-weather utility platform.
traitReasons.maintenanceSimplicity: A rigid frame/fork avoids suspension service, although the road drivetrain and hydraulic brakes still require maintenance.
traitReasons.suspensionCapability: Road R1 is intentionally rigid and has no suspension travel.

generalTradeoffs: Less impact isolation on rough surfaces

traitReasons.pavedEfficiency: MTB M1 can ride pavement, but wide tires, suspension and trail geometry trade some paved efficiency for control.
traitReasons.mixedSurface: Large-volume tires and trail-oriented geometry cope well with changing and rough surfaces.
traitReasons.technicalTerrain: Full suspension, trail geometry, wide tires and strong braking are built around technical terrain control.
traitReasons.distanceEfficiency: It can cover distance, but the trail setup is not optimized for sustained paved-speed efficiency.
traitReasons.climbingCapability: Wide gearing and traction support steep climbing, though the platform prioritizes trail capability over road efficiency.
traitReasons.comfortControl: Suspension, wide tires, flat-bar leverage and a dropper give strong control on uneven terrain.
traitReasons.cargoUtility: The current MTB M1 reference has no dedicated rack/cargo architecture.
traitReasons.allWeather: Hydraulic discs and off-road tires suit changing conditions better than the Road R1 reference, without making it a utility bike.
traitReasons.maintenanceSimplicity: Fork, rear shock, linkage pivots and dropper post add service complexity.
traitReasons.suspensionCapability: MTB M1 provides both front and rear suspension for rough-terrain wheel control.
